physics_goals.quote: These capabilities are being used in a broad program to study the structure and interactions of nucleons, nuclei, and mesons
physics_goals.value: Study the structure and interactions of nucleons, nuclei and mesons with polarised and unpolarised electron beams and targets up to 11 GeV

summary.plain: CLAS12 is the upgraded Hall B detector at Jefferson Lab for the 12 GeV electron beam. Its magnets and chambers follow the particles from electron collisions with protons and nuclei to study how the proton, neutron and heavier states are built from quarks and gluons.
summary.technical: CLAS12: dual-magnet large-acceptance spectrometer in CEBAF Hall B (superconducting torus for forward angles up to 35 degrees, solenoid and central tracker for 35-125 degrees) with 1% / 3% forward / central momentum resolution; running since February 2018 with polarised electron beams up to 11 GeV on polarised and unpolarised targets (DVCS, SIDIS, TMDs, hadron spectroscopy).

unique_capabilities.quote: CLAS12 is based on a dual-magnet system with a superconducting torus magnet that provides a largely azimuthal field distribution that covers the forward polar angle range up to 35
unique_capabilities.value: Dual-magnet system: superconducting torus for the forward region and solenoid with central tracker for large angles, with good particle identification and high data-acquisition rates
